title: Core-Zone Sinusoidal Perturbation on 21-Layer Defect Cavity
scientific_hypothesis: Applying constrained sinusoidal thickness perturbation (±3 nm) exclusively to layers 5-13 in the core chirp zone will fine-tune local effective refractive index steps, widening stopband margin while preserving the central resonance peak at 1550 nm.
design_principle: Defective DBR bandpass filter with quarter-wave DBR mirrors and half-wave defect cavity. Local thickness modulation in the transition region between mirrors and cavity controls stopband edge steepness without shifting center wavelength.
proposed_topology: 21 finite coating layers: [Ta2O5|SiO2]×10|Ta2O5(cavity)|[SiO2|Ta2O5]×10 on Fused Silica substrate, air incident
design_variables: layer thicknesses with layers 5-13 initialized from iteration_16 candidate 3 and perturbed ±3 nm sinusoidally
manufacturing_considerations: ±3 nm perturbation within typical deposition tolerance
theory_basis: Defect mode transmittance depends on background refractive index matching and cavity thickness precision
Local index step modulation affects stopband edge steepness in DBR structures
expected_advantages: Preserves verified 0.9831 score baseline from iteration_16
Targeted perturbation reduces search space while exploring local optimum
Maintains central resonance while potentially improving stopband suppression
known_risks: Sinusoidal pattern may not match optimal perturbation profile
Limited perturbation magnitude may be insufficient to escape local optimum
Core zone layer selection (5-13) may not capture most sensitive regions
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer defect-cavity bandpass filter using Ta2O5 and SiO2 on Fused Silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: Ta2O5(1)|SiO2(2)|Ta2O5(3)|SiO2(4)|Ta2O5(5)|SiO2(6)|Ta2O5(7)|SiO2(8)|Ta2O5(9)|SiO2(10)|Ta2O5(11-cavity)|SiO2(12)|Ta2O5(13)|SiO2(14)|Ta2O5(15)|SiO2(16)|Ta2O5(17)|SiO2(18)|Ta2O5(19)|SiO2(20)|Ta2O5(21). Initialize thicknesses from iteration_16 gradient_thickness_03 candidate: [250.456, 288.503, 233.021, 296.316, 233.533, 271.065, 152.587, 333.157, 113.740, 196.749, 529.185, 249.863, 114.912, 186.653, 166.195, 307.354, 107.020, 246.445, 160.804, 305.151, 238.675] nm. Apply sinusoidal perturbation with amplitude 3 nm and period spanning layers 5-13 to those layers only. Optimize all layer thicknesses with bounds 50-350 nm for non-cavity layers and 400-650 nm for cavity layer. Evaluate coherent TMM transmittance at normal incidence across 1400-1700 nm wavelength range. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Following insight appendage guidance to apply targeted sinusoidal perturbation on core chirp zone layers 5-13 using iteration_16 candidate 3 thickness vector as scaffold, aiming to widen stopband margin while preserving central resonance.
